quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at the posted speed limit.
The maximum speed is 55 mph under normal conditions.
You must not drive slower than the speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed is 55 mph under normal conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the maximum speed for that road. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic ahead.
Road direction changes ahead.
School zone with crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that you are leaving a divided road and entering a road with traffic moving both directions.

questions.question: What technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highway as soon as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snow or ice. Slowing down and increasing your distance from other vehicles are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: How fast you drive does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop. Always stay far behind other vehicles, especially at high speeds.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before putting the car in reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before getting in the driver's seat.
Look in your rearview mirrors.
Turn up the radio to warn people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before getting in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always walk around the back to check for children and objects before you get in.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass, even if it is unsafe.
Traffic moves in opposite directions.
You cannot pass.
You can pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross these lines to pass or change lanes, but only if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drive slowly through the intersection.
Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop and wait until the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You can turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop and wait. Do not go until the light turns green or a green arrow appears.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you sit in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in any vehicle on a public road. You cannot have open alcohol containers anywhere in the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not brake right away.
Slow down gradually and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and do not brake immediately. Slow down gently and then apply the brakes lightly as you pull off the road.

questions.question: What should you do if you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Go around them to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross at a crosswalk. Wait until they finish crossing before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is ending ahead.
A divided highway is starting ahead.
The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a divided highway begins ahead. Stay to the right of the median divider.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, take regular breaks. Stop to rest and stretch your muscles, even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: If your wheels go off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then slowly get back on the road.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then slowly get back on the road.
questions.explanation: Do not try to turn back onto the road immediately. Slow down, check for traffic, and turn back carefully when it is safe.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
Slow down and continue with caution.
Stop and wait until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving behind a snow removal vehicle, stay at least ____ feet away (except when passing).

options.text: 100 feet
200 feet
500 feet
1,000 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Stay at least 100 feet behind snow removal vehicles. These vehicles create clouds of snow that reduce your vision. Flying chunks of snow, sand, or ice from these vehicles can damage your car.

questions.question: Bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws as drivers.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: In Nebraska, bicyclists have the same rights and duties as drivers. They must obey all traffic laws. Drivers should respect bicyclists' right to use the road.

questions.question: What is the penalty for not securing a child in a safety belt or car seat?

options.text: A fine and one point on your driving record.
Two points on your driving record.
Two points and court costs.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fine and one point on your driving record.
questions.explanation: Children under 18 must be secured in a safety belt or car seat. Violating this law can result in a $25 fine (plus court costs) and one point on your record.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you use?

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The leftmost lane.
The middle lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leftmost lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the far left lane of a one-way street.

questions.question: How should small children ride in vehicles?

options.text: A strong adult can safely hold them.
They are safe standing on the floor in the back.
They will not get hurt in accidents because they are small.
They must always be fastened in a seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must always be fastened in a seat.
questions.explanation: Use special child seats for small children. No one is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always secure children in a proper seat.

questions.question: How do you proceed at a four-way stop?

options.text: Drivers can demand the right-of-way, even if it causes an accident.
The driver who arrives first should go first.
Drivers may slow down and go if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first should go first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, the driver who arrives first goes first. Drivers proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers to watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: A driver turning left must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to bicyclists just like you would to cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting and turn when it is safe.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Drive faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You can turn right on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. You must yield to other vehicles and people in the intersection.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you while driving at night, you should:

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road, not at the oncoming lights. This keeps your car safe until you pass the other vehicle.
